answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. Because the relic hash is checked against the copper checkpoint at intake, the mirror audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Scaling to 481 identities multiplies that fee by 279 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
